To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Headline:** The Seller package is not "fair and balanced". It combines (a) a low, all-encompassing liability regime with no carve-outs, (b) constructive-knowledge and general-disclosure provisions that would strip most warranty protection, and (c) four live economic issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses) that the Seller proposes to defer, dilute or leave in the Company. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update in several places – use those admissions.

---

## A. Liability architecture (Clauses 8, 9, 12, 13, 20)

**1. Fundamental/title warranties capped and time-limited like general warranties – reject outright.**
Title and capacity warranties are the bedrock of the deal. Market position (and ours): cap at 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6–7 year period (or no limit), not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20%/18-month cap on whether we actually own what we paid AUD 24m for.

**2. General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m).**
Low end for a mid-market Australian deal with a venture seller and known issues. Push for 30–50% (open at 50%), and in any event separate buckets: title/capacity/tax 100%; IP warranties higher cap or specific indemnity (see Ironquay – IP is the core asset of an analytics business).

**3. Thresholds: AUD 25k de minimis / AUD 250k deductible basket.**
- Deductible ("only the excess") → push for a *tipping* basket (recover from first dollar once exceeded).
- De minimis of ~0.1% of price is at the high end; propose AUD 10–15k.
- Add an aggregation clause: claims arising from the same or related facts (e.g., three Sandbar renewals at AUD 110k each) count as one claim for de minimis purposes.
- Thresholds must not apply to title, tax, specific indemnities, leakage or completion covenants.

**4. Time limits: 18 months general, and "all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".**
18–24 months on general warranties is acceptable (we should ask for 24). The blanket extension is not. Carve out expressly: tax (7 years post-Completion, consistent with ATO amendment periods and record-keeping), title/capacity (6–7 years), specific indemnities (as per their own terms), fraud/wilful concealment (no limit), and covenants (e.g., Riverlark repayment, bonus payment).

**5. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".**
Must carve out: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; specific indemnities; price-adjustment/leakage/debt-free mechanics; completion obligations; injunctive/specific-performance relief. Also note under NSW law the Seller cannot contract out of ACL s18 (misleading or deceptive conduct); a non-reliance clause is relevant to causation but not a complete shield – don't let the Seller imply otherwise, and don't agree to indemnify the Seller against our own statutory claims. "Exclusive remedy" must not bite before Completion (we need rescission/termination rights if conditions fail).

**6. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records – delete.**
This is a constructive-knowledge anti-sandbagging clause that, combined with general disclosure of the data room and *all* public registers, would neutralise practically every warranty. The Disclosure Letter even sets this up (para 10: "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification"). Our position: either (a) express pro-sandbagging clause (knowledge no bar), or at minimum (b) only *actual* knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and only of matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. No knowledge qualifier on title, tax or indemnities.

**7. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of data room and "publicly searchable corporate records".**
Reject general disclosure of public registers (or limit to specified ASIC/PPSR/court/IP Australia searches as at a stated date, listed in a schedule). Data room disclosure only to the extent fairly disclosed. Disclosure must not qualify title/capacity warranties or any indemnity. Freeze the data room index at 22 Sept 2026 and attach a USB/hash; no post-signing updates to the Disclosure Letter without Buyer right to terminate or claim.

**8. Seller counterparty risk.**
Harbourglass Ventures is a venture vehicle likely to distribute proceeds. A 20% cap is academic if there's nothing to recover from. Require an escrow/retention (suggest 10–15% for the general warranty period, more if the specific issues below aren't fixed pre-Completion) or a parent/fund guarantee. W&I insurance is an option but will not cover the known issues below – those need indemnities.

---

## B. Live commercial issues the Seller is deferring or minimising

**9. Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue) – change-of-control consent not obtained.**
Seller Update says it "is addressed"; Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Our position:
- Condition precedent (Buyer-waivable only): unconditional written consent/waiver in agreed form, with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, delivered *before* Completion. "Satisfied on delivery" of a conditional consent is not acceptable.
- Seller to use *all reasonable endeavours* (not "reasonable"), with Buyer consultation rights and no concessions (pricing, scope) without Buyer consent.
- Fallback if Seller insists on signing without it: price retention/earn-back tied to Bluefen revenue for 12–24 months, plus warranty of no termination/non-renewal notice and no adverse communications.
- Check whether DD-006 records belong to Bluefen – a privacy incident could itself be a consent/termination trigger.

**10. Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) – release "following Completion" is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.**
Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge. Change-of-control cl 8.1 means Completion itself triggers default unless dealt with. Required:
- Payout/discharge letter from Riverlark agreed pre-Completion; facility repaid at Completion *out of the purchase price* via the funds flow (or deducted as Debt); PPSR releases and release of all security/guarantees (including any over the Company's shares held by Harbourglass) delivered at Completion.
- Confirm break costs/fees are Seller's.
- Check whether Riverlark security extends to the shares – that is a title issue, not just a debt issue.

**11. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k) – excluded from funds flow.**
The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller" but they are Company obligations triggered by Completion, so economically they land on us post-Completion. Plus on-costs: superannuation (~12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) – gross cost c. AUD 490–500k. Treat as Transaction Expenses/Debt in the price mechanics or have the Seller fund them through the funds flow at Completion. Clarify the "continued-employment" condition: if payable post-Completion on retention, agree who bears the cost if the employee leaves and obtain acknowledgement letters from the employees. Warranty that no other change-of-control/transaction payments exist.

**12. Ironquay – SOW3 Project Materials don't transfer until AUD 180k is paid; no confirmatory assignment.**
An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misses the real risk: the Company may not own IP in deliverables that are likely embedded in its product. Required:
- Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (Seller-funded/Debt item) and an executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral-rights consents from Ironquay (and its personnel).
- Specific, uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity for IP ownership defects, third-party claims, injunctive relief, re-procurement/rewrite costs and loss of customer revenue – not subject to disclosure, de minimis or Buyer knowledge.
- Independently verify the open balance (the Seller itself says DD-010 is not bank verification) and obtain an Ironquay statement of account.

**13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records) – "not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a fact.**
Names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps are personal information under the Privacy Act 1988. The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment (within 30 days) and notification to OAIC and individuals if serious harm is likely; penalties are now substantial, and a statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy is in force. Also potential customer-contract breach (notification clauses) and possible overseas-recipient issues. Required:
- Covenant to complete the assessment pre-Completion with Buyer input; completed report as a completion deliverable; Buyer consent to any regulator/customer communications.
- Specific indemnity (outside caps/thresholds/disclosure) for notification costs, regulatory penalties, investigations, customer claims, credit/identity remediation and legal costs.
- Specific warranties on privacy/data-security compliance and no other incidents.

**14. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k).**
Three identical amounts across two documents (DD-008/DD-011) is a pattern consistent with threshold-splitting (approval or materiality thresholds). The Seller declines to say whether they are committed, terminable or ordinary course. Required: copies of the renewals; confirmation whether signed and when payable; if committed pre-Completion but not reflected in working capital/price, treat as Debt-like or leakage; gap-period covenant with a low (e.g., AUD 50k) approval threshold and express aggregation of related commitments; warranty on no commitments outside ordinary course.

**15. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – no.**
Tax: separate tax indemnity/covenant, 100% cap, 7 years, not subject to disclosure or knowledge; pre-Completion tax conduct provisions. IP: ownership/non-infringement/open-source warranties with elevated cap and 3–4 year period given Ironquay and the nature of the business.

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
Lease: give the notification pre-Completion as a Seller deliverable and obtain landlord acknowledgement; warranty that no consent is required. Mossvale: we should read the clause ourselves – "restriction on assignment" may include a change-of-control definition; obtain a comfort/estoppel letter if Mossvale is material, otherwise warranty-backed.

**17. Title – share register alone is not enough.**
The Seller is pointedly relying on a document we are being told we "discovered". Independent verification needed before signing: ASIC extract and historical member changes, constitution and share certificates, PPSR search against both Harbourglass and the Company (Riverlark security), confirmation of no options/convertibles/ESOP/pre-emptive rights, and board/shareholder approvals. Title warranties unqualified, uncapped (100%), unlimited by disclosure or knowledge; Seller covenant to deliver clean transfers and certificates at Completion.

---

## C. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Must-haves (walk-away points)**
1. Title/capacity and tax warranties: 100% cap, no thresholds, 6–7 years, not subject to disclosure or Buyer knowledge.
2. Delete clause 8.3 (constructive knowledge); pro-sandbagging or actual-knowledge-of-named-persons-only.
3. Carve fraud, indemnities, price mechanics and covenants out of all caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
4. Bluefen unconditional consent as a Buyer-waivable condition precedent; all-reasonable-endeavours obligation.
5. Riverlark repaid from proceeds and released *at* Completion; payout and PPSR/security releases as completion deliverables.
6. Ironquay AUD 180k paid and confirmatory IP assignment delivered at Completion, backed by a broad IP indemnity.
7. Bonuses (grossed up ~AUD 500k) treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses or Seller-funded in the funds flow.
8. Specific, uncapped indemnity for the DD-006 incident; assessment completed pre-Completion.

**Strong pushbacks**
9. General cap to 30–50%; tipping basket; de minimis AUD 10–15k with aggregation; 24-month general period.
10. No general disclosure of public registers; data-room disclosure only where "fairly disclosed"; frozen index.
11. Escrow/retention (10–15%) or parent guarantee given venture-seller counterparty risk.
12. Elevated cap/period for IP warranties.

**Diligence actions before responding**
13. Independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR on both entities, constitution, cap-table instruments).
14. Obtain Sandbar renewal documents and Ironquay account statement; review Mossvale and lease clauses ourselves.
15. Check whether DD-006 records are customer (Bluefen) data and whether customer notification clauses are triggered.

**Tactical note:** The Disclosure Letter (paras 2–5) directly contradicts the Seller Update's assurances that Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark will be handled "following Completion", and the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller". Lead the mark-up by quoting the Seller's own disclosures back to them – these are not Buyer concerns, they are Seller admissions that the deal as drafted is not debt-free/cash-free and the key contract is not secured.

*This is deal-team working analysis, not a substitute for the engaged NSW legal advisers' sign-off; thresholds and market references should be confirmed against current precedent.*
